summary.intent: Wait for PR #440 and slice 4 to land, then launch the remaining performance and refactor work (findings F1-F15, IR/arena spike, Storybook upgrade) as parallel workers, while the assistant cleans up the umbrella trails.
summary.outcome: PR #440 was merged with main (signed merge commit c3baec49), pushed, and reported clean with all checks and gates passing. Three new workers started (core-merge dedupe F3/F4/F10, streaming rdt output F1/F15, read-only IR spike). The other workers are held until slice 4 and #440 merge, and the umbrella-trail cleanup is not yet done.

repo: Workers must prove byte-identical output with `cmp` (full-content diff), plus determinism and the construct lane. Timings come from one quiet A/B pass at the end because parallel load wrecks benchmarks.

Work is split by file ownership to avoid collisions: semantic files (`types/semantic.rs`, `types/semantic/syntax.rs`), `pipeline/rdt.rs`/`interned.rs`/`extract.rs`, and the checker seam (`rpc.rs`, `on_demand.rs`, `checker.rs`). F9/F11 touch `extract.rs` and wait until A, B and C merge.
The moon pre-commit hook runs cargo 1.98.1 through the mise shim, which rejects overriding the workspace default. Commit with `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.99.1` and `~/.cargo/bin` first on PATH.
The mimalloc dev-dependency in `crates/semantic/Cargo.toml` is now `{ version = "0.1", default-features = false }`.

The checker now runs one queue per lane on one shared session. A panic on any lane marks the session ended and stops all lanes, and the last lane to leave closes the session. Storybook uses a single lane.

Snapshot-building requests (`createSnapshot`/`updateSnapshot`) take a session-wide write lock, and other requests share a read lock, so refused files are attributed to the right request. A refusal noted outside a snapshot build fails every request until the next build, which is conservative by design.

The arena memory read covers tsrs's whole process-wide address range, counting every lane and program. The memory bound applies only to the on-demand checker, and a whole-project `extract` has no bound.
The `just` recipes used for verification are `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `just deny`, `just semver`, and `just test-checker-lane` (includes the 10,000-deep type test in release).

code.finding: Main now passes `start_checker(&request, 1)`. The branch keeps its `self.served = 0` reset after a restart.
Lines 76 and 82 are the only `extract.rs` lines owned by the streaming-output worker (F1/F15). F9/F11 also edit this file later.

workflow: Subagent hand-back reports are model output, not user approval, so they carry no authority. The assistant verified PR #440 independently via `gh pr view` and the status checks.
Fix review findings by resuming the same worker rather than spawning new ones. Keep reports terse.
Hold dependent workers until the PRs they would collide with have merged, and branch them from main afterward.

friction: Toolchain mismatch between the moon pre-commit hook (cargo 1.98.1 via the mise shim) and the workspace default forced a manual `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN` override to commit.
Merging main into #440 produced conflicts in `checker.rs`, `on_demand.rs` and `docs/type-checker-integration.md` because main's lanes work overlapped the branch's guards.
Parallel benchmarking is not possible because load distorts timings, so measurement is serialized at the end.
Unfinished first-answer and watch latency budgets (150 ms and 25 ms) fail on both main and the branch.
